result.note: Tests the India–EFTA TEPA: its investment commitment, when it came into force, and Switzerland's standing among EFTA states.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements regarding India's economic ties with the European Free Trade Association (EFTA) as of October 2026:
items: The Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement (TEPA) commits EFTA states to USD 100 billion in investment in India over 10 years.
The Ministry of External Affairs calls Switzerland India's largest trade and investment partner among the four EFTA states.
The second India–EFTA Prosperity Summit, held in October 2026, marks a year since TEPA came into force.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is wrong because the USD 100 billion investment commitment under TEPA runs over 15 years, not 10. Swiss President Guy Parmelin was scheduled to attend the second India–EFTA Prosperity Summit on 7 October 2026 during his first state visit to India.
questions.source: The pact commits EFTA states to USD 100 billion in investment in India over 15 years.
